name: The Oak of Laukiai

location.address: Ąžuolo g. 9, Rukai village, Šačiai eldership, Skuodas District Municipality
location.neighbourhood: Rukai, Skuodas district (roughly 18 km by road from central Plunge)

access: On the grounds of a private family homestead in Rukai village. The owning family opened the site to the public in 2025 when the community restored it: there is a marked path, a protective fence around the trunk and a free visitor car park on site. No appointment or ticket needed.
transport: No public transport reaches Rukai. Car only, about 18 km (25-30 minutes' drive) from central Plunge; free parking on site.
verify_notes: 2026 European Tree of the Year, WINNER (1st place, 6,153 tree points, first Lithuanian win in the contest's 15-year history), beating Slovakia's Old Wild Apple Tree (4,766 pts) and Poland's elm 'Crooked Tree' (4,720 pts). Also won Lithuania's own 'Tree of the Year 2025' title (3,436 votes among 23 nominees), run by the Lietuvos arboristikos centras (Lithuanian Arboricultural Center) and the Seimas Environment Protection Committee. Species: Pedunculate/Common Oak, Quercus robur. Age not documented exactly; the Lithuanian Arboricultural Center's own page (national contest organizer, arboristai.lt) states 'unknown, estimated at about 350-400 years' -- source says this explicitly, not a derived estimate by us. LRT (national broadcaster) independently calls it a tree 'spanning four centuries' (400 metus skaiciuojantis) and says it was planted more than 350 years ago by the Laukiai family. Measurements per arboristai.lt: girth 5.10 m at 1.3 m height, height about 27.0 m, crown width 28.35 m. Coordinates match almost exactly across the contest page (N 56 10'34.9'', E 21 40'17.59'') and arboristai.lt (56.176362, 21.671554); tree-level precision, confirmed. STORY: planted over 350 years ago by Pranciskus and Barbora Laukiai; the tree grew alongside the family through six generations (named sons/descendants down to the present owners); local legend holds each generation came to sit against it in silence. It stood half-forgotten, known only to the village, until 2025, when the Rukai village community restored the surrounding ground: cleared it, laid paths, sowed grass, fenced the trunk for protection and built a car park, and the homestead's owner opened the space to the public. The community also planted more than 40 young oaks beside it, calling the new grove 'Rasos parkas' (Dawn's Park), a continuity-of-generations planting. Winner was announced in the European Parliament in Brussels, March 2026; a change to the contest's voting formula (to favour smaller countries) is credited with letting Lithuania win for the first time. Address given as 'Azuolo g. 9-9A, Rukai, Skuodo r.' by the Skuodas tourism office and 'Azuolo g. 9, Rukai village, Saciai eldership, Skuodas district municipality' by arboristai.lt; same site, minor address variance, not a discrepancy about the tree itself. ACCESS CAVEAT for the writer: this is private homestead land voluntarily opened by its owner, not a municipal park; the honest framing is 'on private grounds, opened to visitors' rather than 'public park'. DISTANCE CAVEAT: Rukai/Laukiai sits about 18km from Plunge's town centre and further still from Plunge's existing walkable tree cluster (Plunge's other trees span a claimed 19.3km already); this is a separate car stop, not part of the same walk, and the page should say so honestly rather than imply one afternoon on foot covers all seven trees.
